name: Abaco Boat Rental
brand_truth: One boat, done right: identical 24 ft Key Wests kept on Man-O-War Cay and delivered to your dock.
buyer: Families and friends (mostly US) staying a week on Elbow Cay, Hope Town, Guana Cay or Marsh Harbour, planning on a phone, comparing other Abaco rentals on boat condition, delivery hassle and the real total.

direction.why: They rent exactly one object, so the boat and its price are the hero. Deep blue field frames their overcast boat photo; one sun-yellow accent for the action. Unlike Donny's horizontal journey and time rail.

design.signature: A day ruler on the first screen rolls the published day rate; one running estimate (days, delivery cay, add-ons) follows the visitor to their Booqable page or a prefilled WhatsApp message

concept_type: booking: one boat, day-rate and delivery estimate, handing off to their live Booqable booking page
tier_visual_why: A rental of one stock boat is explained by price and delivery, not by geometry, so no real-time 3D. The wow is type, the rolling price ruler and one living-water photograph (a small shader over their own photo, three.js loaded lazily, paused off screen).

images.credit: abacoboatrental.com (844 x 844 px source, shown at 620 css px or less)

critic.by: independent critic mode 2, after one fix pass

current_site_findings: Homepage hero shows 'Unable to load video. Try again later.'
Only one real boat photo; pages open with a video, an Unsplash stock photo and a swimming pig
No price on the homepage; rates, delivery and add-ons are plain text on an inner page
Nobody can total a trip (days, delivery both ways, extras)
Empty homepage meta description; title is only the name
pitch_line: Your rates are your best argument and they are a click away as plain text. Here a family drags to seven days, taps Hope Town, sees the whole price and lands on your booking page in under a minute.
assumptions: Estimate uses the published rates, VAT excluded; snorkel sets priced at the 'from $5 a day' floor
The free crew-return option is offered for Elbow Cay and Marsh Harbour only, as their rates page states (Hope Town is listed separately at $100 each way)
The ruler stops at 14 days; longer rentals keep the $303 rate
Guest notes are verbatim excerpts from their homepage, unnamed, labelled as such
The sea-life photos are on their site but may be stock: confirm rights, or replace with their own
Their boat photo is small (844 px): a new shoot of the boat would lift the whole page
notes: awaiting independent critic. BLIND: the sandbox blocks outside hosts, so look.mjs references and their live site were not seen; their photos were viewed through a Lovable contact sheet (project b5272829, two rounds, own photos only, nothing generated) and QA screenshots use low-resolution crops of that sheet routed in with page.route, so photos look softer there than live. Audit done this session (Squarespace + Booqable, booking-site, priority B). qa.mjs: 0 blockers; the one warning is the shared concept button (32 px tall). interact.mjs: 18 buttons, 0 dead, 0 JS errors on index; faq.html uses native details, which the tool does not count. distinct.mjs: distinct (closest 66). LivingWater needs CORS from the Squarespace CDN; if refused, the plain photo stays (not verifiable here). Decisions: boat photo kept at 620 css px or less because the source is 844 px; pig photos, Unsplash hero and the Google Maps boundary screenshot not used; reviews shown without names or stars; no aggregateRating. Stitched full-page screenshots hide the fixed tab and concept tag after the first viewport. | 2026-11-21 final check: independent critic (mode 2) first scored photo 3, comp 3, refs 3. One fix pass: boat photo unboxed and bleeding off the right edge (about 720 css px, source 844) with a slow push-in drift, muted text contrast raised, phone stepper removed so the ruler is the one duration control, tiers in one tabular row. Re-score: all 4 except references 3. Left needs-review. Reason: the delivery chips and add-on steppers mid-page read like a form (critic suggests a tappable Sea of Abaco map of cays), the FAQ page reads like paperwork (lead with a large tariff card), and the 7 tick label hides under the ruler thumb.
